text: Bacterial translation initiation relies on initiation factors IF1–IF3 to select the initiator tRNA and start codon in the 30S subunit P site. This study reports 11 single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) reconstructions of the bacterial 30S subunit bound to initiator tRNA, mRNA, and IF1–IF3, capturing distinct steps along the initiation pathway. IF1 provides key anchoring points for IF2 and IF3, enhancing their activities. IF2 positions a domain in an extended conformation suited to capturing the formylmethionyl moiety charged on tRNA. IF3 and tRNA undergo large conformational changes that enable accommodation of formylmethionyl-tRNA (fMet-tRNA(fMet)) into the P site for start codon recognition.
